answer: Reputation-priced fees resist Sybil attacks: every new identity pays a high transaction fee that falls only as it completes attested work across successive epochs, like a reef that grows slowly and a river that carves its bed over time. One honest agent pays the top rate briefly, then earns the discount; a thousand fakes each pay full price forever, since none accumulates history. No shortcut exists - a comet passes once, but reputation pricing demands sustained proof, so a fake swarm costs a thousand full-price fees while honest agents glide on earned discounts.
